subject: Literacy
title: The sound /s/
objectives: Children will hear and say the sound /s/ at the start of words.
Children will find objects that start with /s/ with support.
content: Listening for the sound /s/ at the start of words, finding things that start with /s/, and the /s/ song.
teachingActivities: Say /s/ as a pure sound, a long hiss "sss", with no vowel added; say "the sound sss" and never "es" or "suh"; show your mouth and teeth; use real objects; children hear and say sounds only, with no letter formation.
learnerActivities: Hear and say the sound /s/ at the start of words and point to objects that start with /s/ with support.
resources: A toy sun, a sock, a toy snake, a spoon
assessment: Observe whether each child says /s/ clearly and points to an object that starts with /s/.
expectedOutcomes: Points to an object that starts with /s/.

lessons.title: The snake says sss
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will hear and say the sound /s/ as the snake sound.
successCriteria: Says the sound sss when shown the snake
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear rhyming words, clap the beats in words and join in songs; they have not yet been taught any letter sounds.
resources: A toy snake or a picture of a snake
lessons.starter: Wiggle the toy snake along the mat and say "The snake goes sss." Hold a finger to your lips.
teacherActivities: Say "sss" clearly, a long hissing sound. Show how your teeth come together and the air flows out.
Say "sss" together while the snake wiggles. Say "the sound is sss".
Make the snake go quiet and loud and say sss softly and loudly.
Let each child look in the mirror and say sss.
learnerActivities: Children watch your mouth and listen.
Children say "sss" with you.
Children copy a soft sss and a loud sss.
Child watches their mouth and says sss.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "sss" clearly, a long hissing sound. Show how your teeth come together and the air flows out. Children: Children watch your mouth and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "sss" together while the snake wiggles. Say "the sound is sss". Children: Children say "sss" with you.
Step 3. Teacher: Make the snake go quiet and loud and say sss softly and loudly. Children: Children copy a soft sss and a loud sss.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child look in the mirror and say sss. Children: Child watches their mouth and says sss.

practical.title: Snake sound
steps: Give each child a pretend snake made from a scarf or a hand.
Wiggle the snake along the floor and say sss.
Stop the snake and listen quietly.
practical.safety: Use a soft toy snake and tell children it is a toy. Keep the sound gentle and do not let children blow hard to avoid dizziness.

differentiation.support: Wiggle the snake with the child and say sss together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend what the snake says.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you make a long sss?
questions.expected: Child makes a long hissing sound.

lessons.conclusion: Settle the snake to sleep with a very quiet sss.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a snake sound at home, a long sss, and wiggle a hand like a snake.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hear and say the sound /s/ as the snake sound" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: The snake says sss, sss, sss. The snake says sss, sss, sss.

lessons.title: Sun, sock and spoon
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will hear that sun, sock and spoon start with the sound /s/.
successCriteria: Repeats the word and the first sound
Points to an object that starts with /s/
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear rhyming words, clap the beats in words and join in songs; they have not yet been taught any letter sounds.
resources: A toy sun, a sock, a spoon
lessons.starter: Hold up the sun and say "Sun. Sss-un. It starts with sss." Show the sock and say "Sock. Sss-ock."
teacherActivities: Say each word slowly and stress the first sound: sss-un, sss-ock, sss-poon.
Put the three objects on a tray and say "These all start with sss."
Add a ball to the tray and ask "Does ball start with sss?"
Let each child pick an s-object and say the word.
learnerActivities: Children repeat the word and the first sound.
Children touch each object and say sss.
Child shakes their head or says no.
Child picks and says sss and the word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say each word slowly and stress the first sound: sss-un, sss-ock, sss-poon. Children: Children repeat the word and the first sound.
Step 2. Teacher: Put the three objects on a tray and say "These all start with sss." Children: Children touch each object and say sss.
Step 3. Teacher: Add a ball to the tray and ask "Does ball start with sss?" Children: Child shakes their head or says no.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick an s-object and say the word. Children: Child picks and says sss and the word.

practical.title: S tray
steps: Put the sun, sock, spoon and a ball on a tray.
Ask each child to take an object that starts with sss.
Say the word and the first sound.
practical.safety: Use large, clean objects. Keep the spoon plastic and blunt. Supervise handling.

differentiation.support: Offer two objects, one that starts with sss, and say the sound first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another sss object in the classroom.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What sound does sun start with?

expectedOutcomes: Hears /s/ at the start of words
Picks objects that start with /s/ with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects in the bag and say sss.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for things that start with sss, such as a sock or a spoon, and say the sound.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hear that sun, sock and spoon start with the sound /s/" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?

lessons.title: The sss song
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will sing a song about the sound /s/ with actions.
successCriteria: Sings or hums the sss song
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear rhyming words, clap the beats in words and join in songs; they have not yet been taught any letter sounds.
lessons.starter: Wiggle the snake and sing "sss, sss, sss". Ask "Who knows the snake song?"
teacherActivities: Sing the song slowly: "Sss, sss, sss, sun and sock and snake. Sss, sss, sss, what can you take?" Show the cards.
Sing again and do the snake action with your arm.
Sing again and let children hold up a card at the right word.
Let a child lead the song with the snake.
learnerActivities: Children listen and look at the cards.
Children copy the snake action and the sound.
Child holds up the sun, sock or snake card.
Child leads and friends sing.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing the song slowly: "Sss, sss, sss, sun and sock and snake. Sss, sss, sss, what can you take?" Show the cards. Children: Children listen and look at the cards.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing again and do the snake action with your arm. Children: Children copy the snake action and the sound.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing again and let children hold up a card at the right word. Children: Child holds up the sun, sock or snake card.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child lead the song with the snake. Children: Child leads and friends sing.

practical.title: Sing and slither
steps: Give each child a scarf snake.
Sing the song and move the scarf.
Hold up a picture card at each word.
practical.safety: Clear the floor so children can move freely. Keep the volume gentle.

differentiation.support: Sing softly with the child and do the actions together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sing the song to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Sings the sss song with actions
lessons.conclusion: Sing a quiet last verse and put the snake to bed.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing the sss song at home and wiggle like a snake.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sing a song about the sound /s/ with actions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Find the sss things
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will find objects that start with /s/ in a sound hunt.
successCriteria: Says the word and the sound
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear rhyming words, clap the beats in words and join in songs; they have not yet been taught any letter sounds.
resources: Six objects, three starting with /s/ and three that do not
lessons.starter: Say "Let us hunt for sss things. Sss, sss, sss." Show the empty basket.
teacherActivities: Hide the objects around the room in easy places.
Say "Find a sss thing" and let each child look.
Ask "Does it start with sss?" and say the word.
Put the sss things in the basket and the others on the mat.
learnerActivities: Children watch where you put the objects.
Child finds an object and brings it back.
Child says yes or no and the word.
Child sorts the objects.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hide the objects around the room in easy places. Children: Children watch where you put the objects.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Find a sss thing" and let each child look. Children: Child finds an object and brings it back.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Does it start with sss?" and say the word. Children: Child says yes or no and the word.
Step 4. Teacher: Put the sss things in the basket and the others on the mat. Children: Child sorts the objects.

practical.title: Sss hunt
steps: Hide six objects in easy places in the room.
Children find objects and bring them to the mat.
Sort the sss objects into the basket.
practical.safety: Hide objects only in clear, low places away from hazards. Supervise the search and keep children together.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child and point to the object after saying the sound.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to hide an s-object for a friend to find.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Finds objects starting with /s/ with support
lessons.conclusion: Count the objects in the basket and say sss.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a sound hunt at home for things that start with sss.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find objects that start with /s/ in a sound hunt" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

lessons.title: Week 1 sss check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child hears and says /s/.
successCriteria: Points to an object that starts with /s/
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear rhyming words, clap the beats in words and join in songs; they have not yet been taught any letter sounds.
lessons.starter: Wiggle the snake and say "sss". Show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: snake sound, s-objects and the song.
At each station ask "What sound?" and "Which one starts with sss?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child says sss and points.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: snake sound, s-objects and the song. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What sound?" and "Which one starts with sss?" Children: Child says sss and points.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Sound stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use large, clean objects.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to name two more sss words.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says /s/ clearly; points to an object starting with /s/; joins in the song.

questions.question: What sound does the snake make?
Show me something that starts with sss.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the snake with a soft sss.
lessons.homeConnection: Play sound games at home with the sound sss.
